title: A holder or worktree change is never reported as a source change: the first turn's last_reported starts from that turn's own basis, so passed checks stay stale_source_revision
outcome:
When a run's source moves to a new revision between turns (a new holder, or a new named worktree, with content different from the run's last reported source), TermAl reports that change to Engram before any check in the new turn. A check that passes on the new revision then satisfies the run's open test obligations.

Diagnosed by Engram::Coder (TermAl mailbox 62e0c56d #110, 2026-10-01 08:16Z, Engram item w-f263747eac87) on TermAl w-2ccd39a4ff5a. Prior holder's last flagged mutation: observation 71, revision a433, on the old root. New holder Termal::Coder's integrated root: c96ce116, seen only as quiet sightings 105/106 (source_changed: false). Verification 1c96c01b passed at c96ce116 and was assessed stale_source_revision on all 5 open rows (triggers 11, 13, 51, 65, 71).

Engram's verdict: the unbound matcher is right to keep comparing against the latest flagged mutation. A quiet sighting states "no new mutation" and must not displace old obligations. The defect is on TermAl's side. engram_turn_report, as on master 2696e6f, initializes last_reported from the current turn's start basis instead of the run's prior reported basis. So a transition that is already present when the turn starts never produces the change report. Engram::Coder says TermAl must account for the real run-source transition under an admitted mutation grant before the verification, or use the named-root binding and stamping protocol (w-370c). Never fake a filesystem edit, never stamp an old check retrospectively, never retry or waive.
acceptance: A turn whose start revision equals the run's last reported source reports no change; a test covers it.
The full five-stage gate passes on the exact reviewed tree, its run directory and fingerprint cited in a note.

When a turn starts with the run's source at a revision different from the run's last reported source (after a holder or worktree change), TermAl reports that change before any check in the turn, under the admitted mutation grant. A test reproduces Engram::Coder's sequence (old unbound changed R1, then the new holder's quiet R2, then a check passing on R2) and shows the pass stays stale before the fix and satisfies the obligations after it.
